Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same notes and next steps. Please flag any corrections.

Key pain points you shared:
- Strict PII handling across ingestion and storage (names, SSNs, insurance IDs).
- Regulatory requirement to retain audit logs and transaction metadata for at least 2 years; some teams want shorter retention for transcripts.
- Need the ability to produce tamper-evident audit logs for audits and to export logs on demand.
- Preference for redaction at ingest or an automated redaction pipeline before logs are stored.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend app + API gateway on AWS (us-west-2)
- Conversation data stored in S3 (encrypted) and indexed in Elasticsearch
- Internal analytics pipeline (Redshift) for aggregated metrics

Success criteria for a pilot (as we discussed):
1) Demonstrate per-tenant (per-customer) retention policies and easy export of audit logs.
2) Provide configurable PII redaction (ingest-side and on-the-fly) and a clear attestation process.
3) Keep latency and cost within expected limits for 95th percentile interactive use.

Specific asks I noted for follow-up:
- Can Redwood provide a SOC 2 questionnaire and an example audit-log export?
- Clarify options for automatic redaction and whether we can do client-side redaction before sending.
- High-level sizing / cost estimate for a Dedicated pool to support your expected traffic (initial pilot ~10 TPS).

Next steps:
- I will share the SOC 2 questionnaire and a short retention matrix for you to fill out (attached).
- Rishi (SE) will follow up to schedule a technical deep-dive to map logging flows and redaction points.
- Propose pilot timeline: scope & SOW draft by end of next week if you’re comfortable.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Hi Sofia —

Great questions — quick responses below and I attached the SOC 2 questionnaire for your compliance team to review.

- Per-tenant retention: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can enforce per-tenant retention policies at the storage/ingest layer (S3 lifecycle rules + indexing policies). For hosted we offer configurable retention profiles per customer; we can scope a pilot to enforce 90/30/365 day profiles as needed.

- Redaction options: We support three approaches:
  1) Client-side redaction: recommended for highest-sensitivity fields (SDK hooks before payload leaves your environment).
  2) Server-side rule-based redaction: regex/sys patterns applied at ingest.
  3) ML-based redaction pipeline: LLM/NER detector to identify PII with confidence thresholds; can be used in a "redact then store" flow.

  All redaction actions are logged in our audit trail with the reason, rule id, and actor (system vs. client). We can provide a redaction-audit export that shows original masked locations and redaction types.

- Tamper-evident audit logs: We provide exportable audit logs (JSON/NDJSON) with timestamps and HMAC signatures for each batch export. For higher assurance we can support an append-only audit store or deliver signed daily digests for archival. We should scope whether you need cryptographic signing in the pilot SOW.

Attachments: SOC2-questionnaire.pdf (for compliance), data-retention-matrix.xlsx (already sent).

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi to run technical deep-dive with Rajiv and your infra team this week — topics: ingest path, SDK options, where to run client-side redactors, and audit log export format.
- I’ll share a short pilot SOW (scope + success metrics) and a high-level Dedicated sizing estimate by end of week.
- Please confirm 2–3 available 60-minute slots for the SE call (we have Wed 2/18 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2/19 9:00–12:00 PT).

If that works I’ll lock the SE call and route the SOC2 doc to your compliance reviewer.
